headline: Post-tropical rain and strong winds peak today and tonight, then both regions dry out Sunday before a warm Monday
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: The northern rain shield from Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias spreads across Central Kentucky today. Periods of rain, embedded heavier showers and east-northeast gusts of 30–40 mph are possible through the afternoon, followed by additional rain tonight and Sunday morning. Conditions improve west to east Sunday afternoon, with sunny and much warmer weather Monday.

currentConditions.condition: Clear observation beneath increasing regional cloud cover
Clear observation beneath increasing regional cloud cover

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: Official NWS Special Weather Statement for east-northeast gusts of 30–40 mph; independent analysis also identifies localized heavy rain and isolated minor flooding
days.forecast: Cloudy and increasingly windy, with rain becoming more widespread from south to north this morning. Periods of rain continue through tonight, with locally heavier bands possible. Highs should remain in the 60s in most locations. Gusts peak from late morning through the afternoon, then weaken as steadier rain arrives.

days.label: Sunday
days.precipitation: 55–70% through early afternoon; decreasing to 20–40% during the late afternoon and evening
days.hazard: No official NWS watch or warning at issuance; isolated 2–3-inch storm totals, ponding and localized minor flooding remain possible, especially east of Lexington
days.forecast: Periods of rain and a few embedded thunderstorms continue during the morning, then gradually shift east during the afternoon. Weekend rainfall should generally total 0.5–1 inch, with isolated 2–3-inch amounts possible across Central Kentucky and east of I-75. Clouds begin to break from west to east late in the day.

days.label: Monday
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and much warmer as high pressure and upper-level ridging build into the region. Light southwest winds accompany afternoon temperatures near 80 to the lower 80s. Mostly clear and mild conditions continue Monday night.

kentucky.bottomLine: Rain and 30–40 mph gusts are the main concerns today, with additional rain tonight and Sunday morning. Conditions improve Sunday afternoon, followed by sunny and much warmer weather Monday.
kentucky.confidence: High on today's rain and strong-wind window and Monday's dry warmth; moderate-high on Sunday improvement timing; moderate on localized rainfall maxima

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Heavy rain, patchy fog and strong easterly winds are already affecting Clemson and Central. An official Flood Watch continues through 2 PM Sunday and a Wind Advisory through 8 AM Sunday. The heaviest rain and greatest flash-flooding risk should occur this afternoon through early Sunday, while a conditional risk of isolated damaging gusts or brief tornadoes develops tonight if the cold-air wedge weakens.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: Official NWS Flood Watch through 2 PM Sunday and Wind Advisory through 8 AM Sunday; flash flooding, landslides near steep terrain, 30–46 mph gusts, downed limbs and isolated power outages are possible
days.forecast: Cool, cloudy, windy and wet. Heavy rain and patchy fog continue through the day and tonight, with the most intense period from late afternoon through early Sunday. Clemson-area rainfall may total 3–6 inches, while favored Blue Ridge Escarpment locations could receive 5–8 inches. A northward-training band may focus higher totals across parts of the Upstate this evening.

days.label: Sunday
days.precipitation: 30–50% during the morning; 10% or less by afternoon and evening
days.hazard: Official Wind Advisory continues through 8 AM and Flood Watch through 2 PM; an isolated damaging-wind or brief-tornado risk may linger early before shifting east, with residual flooding possible after rain ends
days.forecast: Heavy rain exits during the morning as the remnant circulation accelerates northeast. Patchy fog and residual flooding may persist, but clouds should begin to break during the afternoon. Southwest winds may briefly become gusty as the wedge erodes. Mostly clear and drier weather arrives Sunday night.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No significant weather hazards expected outside isolated gusty northwest winds along the higher Blue Ridge elevations
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and considerably warmer. West winds remain light near Clemson and Central, while some higher ridges may remain breezy. Clear conditions Monday night allow temperatures to settle into the middle to upper 50s.

upstate.bottomLine: The highest-impact period is today through early Sunday: heavy rain, flash-flooding potential, patchy fog and advisory-level winds. A conditional overnight severe-weather threat remains, but the wedge should limit instability in much of the western Upstate. Rapid improvement follows Sunday, with sunny warmth Monday.
upstate.confidence: High on heavy rain, advisory-level winds and Sunday improvement; moderate-high on the flash-flooding corridor; moderate on the overnight severe threat and today's high because wedge strength controls both

College of DuPage Southeast radar mosaic
College of DuPage GOES-East clean infrared

sourceNotes: Official airport observations span 7:15–7:40 AM EDT. Central Kentucky remained dry at observation time, while KCEU reported heavy rain and fog/mist and KLQK reported rain with 0.03 inch in the previous hour. No Tempest observations were used.

The NWS point forecasts were generated at 7:54 AM EDT. Danville has rain chances of 60–70% today and tonight, gusts near 31 mph and a Sunday high near 69°F. Clemson has a 100% rain chance today and tonight, 2–3 inches in each period, gusts near 38–40 mph and a Sunday high near 71°F.

Official hazards are distinct from the independent forecast: Louisville's Special Weather Statement identifies 30–40 mph gusts across much of Central Kentucky; Greenville–Spartanburg's Wind Advisory continues through 8 AM Sunday; and its Flood Watch continues through 2 PM Sunday for Clemson, Central and surrounding Upstate areas.

The final NHC Advisory 15 at 5 AM EDT classified Isaias as post-tropical near 32.0°N, 86.5°W, moving north at 14 mph with 35 mph sustained winds. NHC transferred future advisories to the Weather Prediction Center and emphasized Southeast flash flooding, Southern Appalachian landslides and a Carolinas tornado risk.

Model inventories checked at 7:55 AM EDT showed complete 06Z HRRR through hour 48, 09Z RAP through hour 51, 06Z NAM through hour 84, 06Z NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS through hour 384, 06Z GEFS mean through hour 300 and 00Z ECMWF through hour 360. The 06Z ECMWF cycle was not yet available.

College of DuPage radar at 7:45 AM EDT showed the post-tropical rain shield spreading across the Tennessee Valley, Kentucky, Georgia and the Carolinas, with heavier rain already affecting the Upstate. Clean-infrared imagery at 7:46 AM showed the asymmetric remnant cloud shield and embedded convection extending well east of the inland center.

Short-range temperature panels remain somewhat warmer than official Upstate observations under the rain-cooled wedge. The official observations, point forecast and known warm errors from NAM and RAP during wedge regimes were weighted more heavily, producing a broad 60–70°F Saturday range rather than adopting the warmest deterministic solution.

The GFS and ECMWF agree that the remnant circulation accelerates northeast Sunday, but differ modestly on how quickly the Upstate warms after rain exits. The Sunday ranges retain this uncertainty while Monday confidence is higher under strengthening ridging.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.

The forecast-accuracy summary generated at 3:32 PM EDT October 9 was consulted. KDVK lows were adjusted downward using the updated recommended -1.5°F correction. Upstate low ranges were widened because KCEU retains a recommended +1.5°F correction while KLQK now has a recommended -2.5°F correction. No daytime station correction was applied.

HRRR remains the best overall high-temperature model with a 1.6°F mean absolute error. ECMWF has the best limited cold-air-damming score, while NAM and RAP retain large warm errors in that regime. Ranges were widened because 72-hour coverage is 54.5%, cold-air-damming coverage is 50%, wedge-erosion coverage is 50% and stratiform-precipitation coverage is 37.5%. High rain probabilities remain consistent with the verified 100% observed frequency in the 81–100% bin. This candidate does not modify the repository, forecast archive, website or widget.

appliedAdjustments.details: Shifted the lower portion of overnight ranges downward using KDVK's updated recommended -1.5°F low correction; KLEX remains below the application threshold. No high-temperature station correction was applied. Sunday and Monday ranges were widened because 72-hour coverage is 54.5% and remnant-departure timing affects Sunday temperatures.

Widened overnight ranges in both directions because KCEU has a recommended +1.5°F low correction while KLQK has a recommended -2.5°F correction. HRRR received the greatest overall model weight, but official observations and ECMWF were weighted more heavily for today's wedge because ECMWF has the lowest current cold-air-damming error and HRRR, RAP and NAM run warm in limited wedge samples.
